key_insight: A shallow variational quantum circuit can be trained analytically from the Dirichlet-kernel QPE target distribution to mimic quantum phase estimation without expensive quantum circuit simulation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a hardware-efficient route to molecular energy estimation on NISQ devices by replacing deep QPE circuits with a linearly scaling surrogate.
method: Compute the QPE measurement target classically from the FCI ground-state energy, ancilla count, and evolution time using the Dirichlet kernel.
Train shallow VQC ansätze on IBM Quantum hardware and compare entangler topologies, depths, and dynamical decoupling settings.
Validate surrogate quality with distributional metrics and test chemical-accuracy recovery for H2.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a four-stage hardware study using Hellinger distance, fidelity error, total variation distance, and Jensen-Shannon divergence, with the best configuration recovering ground-state energy within chemical accuracy.
watch_item: Performance depends on hardware noise and ansatz choice, so deeper circuits or mismatched entanglers may reduce fidelity despite the analytic target.
paper_title: An Analytically Trained Variational Surrogate for Quantum Phase Estimation on NISQ Hardware
